findings.title: Recognize spawn-context processes before killing unhealthy workers
findings.body: Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the default-context multiprocessing.Process class. This condition is therefore false for production workers. When a worker hangs, the manager starts a replacement without killing the original and overwrites its tracked reference. The original can remain stuck or resume flushing alongside its replacement. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the actual context's Process class; the termination guard in join() has the same problem.

findings.title: Clean up every worker even after the join deadline expires
findings.body: If next_step.join() consumes the timeout, or waiting for one worker exhausts it, this break skips cleanup of all remaining workers. Setting stopped only requests an exit between flush iterations, so workers blocked in Redis operations or Kafka futures can survive the rebalance and overlap the replacement strategy. The deadline should limit graceful waiting, but every remaining process still needs forced termination and cleanup.

findings.title: Wait for flushing with an unpatched synchronization mechanism
findings.body: test_basic replaces time.sleep with a no-op at line 15, so this added sleep does not wait for the flusher to observe the advanced drift. The following join() sets the worker's stopped flag immediately. Depending on thread scheduling, the worker can exit without emitting the expected segment, leaving the messages assertion flaky. Wait for the produced message or a completion event before joining, using an unpatched synchronization primitive.
